seattle-payroll-expense.name: City of Seattle, payroll expense tax

incomeTax.note: Washington taxes long-term capital gains only. Wages are not taxed.

rules.note: Payroll flag read on paidleave.wa.gov: the 2026 paid leave premium is 1.13% of wages, up to 71.43% of it from the employee, and WA Cares is 0.58% of all wages. Workers also pay part of workers' compensation premiums, at hourly rates that depend on the job. Seattle's payroll expense tax is paid by employers.
notes: Employees pay 0.58% of all wages for the WA Cares long-term care program and up to about 0.81% of wages, up to $184,500, for paid family and medical leave. Workers also pay part of workers' compensation premiums. Not included.

Not included: Washington's Working Families Tax Credit, $335 to $1,330 for 2025 depending on the number of children. It goes to people who qualify for the federal earned income credit and is claimed by a separate application to the Department of Revenue.
maintainerNotes: For 2027 paidleave.wa.gov gives a premium of 1.2% with 70.7% from the employee.
